## Goal

Add `src/feed.ts`, the only module that knows the shape of Wikimedia's featured feed.
It turns the raw `image` field into the `DayImage` record used by the router and client.

## Scope

- `export type DayImage = { date: string; title: string; story: string; credit: string; licence: string; licenceUrl: string; imageUrl: string; thumbUrl: string; width: number; height: number; pageUrl: string; source: "wikimedia" }`.
- `export function feedUrl(date: string): string` converts `YYYY-MM-DD` to the `/YYYY/MM/DD` endpoint.
- `export function normaliseFeed(raw: unknown, date: string): DayImage | null`:
  - reads `raw.image` and returns `null` when it, `image.image.source` or `image.thumbnail.source` is missing;
  - `title` is `image.title` with the leading `File:` and the trailing file extension removed, and underscores replaced by spaces;
  - `story` is `image.description.text`, `credit` is `image.artist.text` (fallback `"Unknown"`), `licence` is `image.license.type` (fallback `"See file page"`), `licenceUrl` is `image.license.url` (fallback `""`), `pageUrl` is `image.file_page`;
  - `width` and `height` come from `image.image`.
- `export async function fetchDay(date: string, fetchImpl: typeof fetch = fetch): Promise<DayImage | null>` requests `feedUrl(date)` with a `user-agent` header and a 5000 ms `AbortSignal.timeout`. It returns `null` on a thrown error, a non-2xx status or a `null` normalisation, and never throws.
- `tests/fixtures/featured.json` is a hand-written feed response with an `image` object holding every field listed above. Tests load it with `readFileSync` and make no network calls.

## Out of scope

- Routing, the image proxy and the offline SVG fallback (W1-03 wires `fetchDay` into the server).
- Thread extraction from the description (a later chunk).

## Done

- `src/feed.ts` exports `DayImage`, `feedUrl`, `normaliseFeed` and `fetchDay` with the signatures above.
- `node --test tests/feed.test.ts` passes with the four tests listed in the header and makes no network calls.
- `src/feed.ts` has no imports outside `node:` built-ins, and relative imports in the test use `.ts` extensions.
- `tests/slice.test.ts` still passes unchanged.
